top.calendar: calendar (group schedule): "id" from the export or the name of the group or calendar; missing — the calendar chosen at the top in “Masses and devotions”
top.calendarName: calendar name — information only (the export writes it, the import ignores it)
top.from: first day of the period "YYYY-MM-DD" — the export writes it; the import reads Masses from that day (missing: from the earliest date in the document)
top.to: last day of the period "YYYY-MM-DD", inclusive
top.masses: Masses, devotions and confession — single and series (below); can be left out when the Masses are already in the calendar
top.occurrences: Masses on specific days with their intentions (below) — the book of intentions goes here

mass.id: "id" from the export — the entry is changed in place (only what the document gives); without "id" a new one is created
mass.key: short name (letters, digits, - and _) — items in "occurrences" point to the entry through "mass": "@name" (e.g. a new one that has no "id" yet)
mass.calendar: calendar of a new entry, when different from the document's calendar (id or name); an existing entry stays in its own
mass.kind: "mass" — Mass (default), "devotion" — devotion (rosary, Way of the Cross…; no intentions), "confession" — confession (no intentions); the import does not change the kind of an existing entry
mass.title: name in the plan and on the notice board (public), e.g. "Children's Mass", "Rosary"; "" — “Mass”, “Devotion”, “Confession”; up to {max} characters
mass.date: day of the Mass or first day of the series "YYYY-MM-DD" (new entry: required)
mass.time: time "HH:MM", local time — 18:00 is six in the evening also after the clock change (new entry: required)
mass.minutes: duration in minutes, 5–1440 (default: Mass {mass} or as in the calendar, confession {confession}, devotion {devotion}); for confession the notice board shows “until …”
mass.repeat: "none" — once (default), "daily" — every day, "weekly" — on chosen weekdays, "monthly" — every month on the same day ("yearly" — every year, may appear in the export)
mass.every: every how many days, weeks or months (1–99, default 1)
mass.weekdays: with "weekly": weekdays {days}; missing — the day of the first date
mass.until: last day of the series "YYYY-MM-DD"; null (or missing in a new series) — no end; an earlier "until" ends the series
mass.place: place, e.g. "cemetery chapel" — encrypted like the place of every date (not on the notice board); "" removes it; up to {max} characters
mass.celebrants: who celebrates the Mass, leads the devotion, hears confession — in the whole series: people of the calendar's group, full name as in the group (e.g. "Fr. John Smith") or a person's id; [] — nobody; at most {max}
mass.changeFrom: only with a series that has an "id": the change applies from this day "YYYY-MM-DD" (this and following) — the old series ends the day before, the new one takes over intentions and people; without "changeFrom" the whole series changes, past Masses too

occurrence.time: time of the Mass "HH:MM" — required without "mass": then the Mass is looked up by day and time among the calendar's Masses
occurrence.mass: which Mass: "id" of an entry from the export's "masses" or "@name" from "key"; missing — by "date" and "time"
occurrence.calendar: calendar, when the document covers several (id or name); missing — the document's calendar
occurrence.free: true — “free”: a Mass without an intention; the import adds nothing (warns when the calendar does have an intention)
occurrence.collective: true — collective Mass: all its intentions without their own "kind" are collective (one priest celebrates them together)
occurrence.cancelled: true — cancel this Mass on this day only (the series stays; not when it has accepted intentions); false — restore a cancelled one
occurrence.celebrants: who celebrates this one Mass — people as in "masses"; missing — unchanged (as in the series)
occurrence.intentions: intentions of this Mass in reading order — text ("For the late John Smith") or an object (below); at most {max}; two single intentions in one Mass mean two priests

intention.id: "id" from the export — the intention is changed in place; written under another Mass (another day or time) — moved there; without "id" — new, unless this Mass already has the same text
intention.text: text read at Mass and posted on the notice board (required, up to {max} characters)
intention.kind: "single" — {single} (default), "collective" — {collective}; for an existing intention missing means: unchanged
intention.status: "accepted" — {accepted} (default), "celebrated" — {celebrated}, "cancelled" — {cancelled} (disappears from the notice board, stays in the office)
intention.giver: who requested it, e.g. "the Smith family, tel. 600 100 200" — encrypted, not on the notice board or the print; up to {max} characters; "" removes it
intention.offering: offering, e.g. "50 zł" — encrypted like the donor; up to {max} characters; "" removes it
intention.celebrant: who celebrates this intention — a person of the group as in "celebrants"; also added to this Mass as celebrant; null or "" — nobody

desc.intro:
Masses, devotions and confession of one calendar (group schedule) with Mass intentions — day by day. The import first shows the list of changes: which Mass on which day gets which intention; it saves only after “Import”.
What the import does (Masses and devotions → “More” → “Import and export (JSON)”):
- An entry with "id" from the export is changed in place — only what the document gives; what it does not give stays. An entry without "id" in "masses" is created new (single or series).
- An intention belongs to a Mass on a SPECIFIC DAY. That Mass is looked up by "mass" (id from the export or "@name" from "masses") and "date" — or by "date" and "time" among the calendar's Masses.
- An intention without "id" is added to its Mass, unless this Mass already has the same text — then nothing is duplicated.
- A Mass that already has ANOTHER intention in the calendar than in the document is a conflict: by default new intentions are not added to it (the warning says which); in the preview you can choose “add beside”.
- Nothing is deleted. "status": "cancelled" withdraws an intention, "until" ends a series, "cancelled": true cancels a Mass on one day.
- The donor and the offering are encrypted in this browser with the key of the calendar's group, the place — with the key of the group that sees the Masses (as for every date). The intention text and the Mass name are public: they are read at Mass and hang on the notice board.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments: at most {masses} entries in "masses", {occurrences} items in "occurrences", {intentions} intentions at one Mass, a period of up to {days} days.

desc.bookText:
The most common work: the parish office copies a month from the book of intentions (e.g. AI from photos of the pages).
1. Easiest to start from the export of that month: every Mass stands in "occurrences" with "date", "time" and "mass" — with the intentions it already has, or with "free": true. Write the intentions into these items (instead of "free": true — "intentions"); do not add or remove items.
2. Without the export: one item for every Mass in the book, with "date" and "time" (the Mass must already be in the calendar or in this document's "masses").
3. “wolna” (free) → "free": true. Several intentions at one Mass → several items in "intentions", in the order of the book. Collective Mass → "collective": true and all its intentions.
4. Copy the text exactly as in the book (“Za śp. …”, “O zdrowie i Boże błogosławieństwo dla …”), without ordinal numbers. An illegible word: the best reading and “[?]” at the end of the text — the office will correct it.
5. Write the donor and the offering only when they are in the book ("giver", "offering"); do not guess.
6. The same text at the same Mass is not added a second time. Another text at a Mass that already has an intention is a conflict — the preview shows it before anything is saved.
Example — the 7:00 and 18:00 Masses are already in the calendar:

desc.usage:
- Masses, devotions and confession are calendar dates: they appear in the Calendar (with the number of intentions at a Mass, e.g. “2 int.”) and in “Now” for everyone who has the key of an area that sees the calendar. People in "celebrants" and "celebrant" find them under “Assigned to me”.
- The parish office works on them in “Masses and devotions”: Intentions, Plan and changes (two weeks), Print.
- The public plan — the page module “Masses and devotions” (also as a widget on another website) — shows without an account the time, name, cancellation, public scheme fields and intention texts (collective ones folded, with their number). It takes Masses only from calendars seen by a public area (“everyone reads”).
- The print for the notice board (Print → “Print intentions (A4)”) is a week of Masses from the same public plan.
- Never in the plan or on the print: donor, offering, place or celebrant; withdrawn intentions ("cancelled") neither — they stay in the office.
- “Celebrated” is not set by itself: the office marks it after Mass (“Mark as celebrated”) or the import does ("status": "celebrated").
- When a Mass gets another time, its intentions stay on the same day; if a day with accepted intentions would disappear, the change is not saved.
- The app does not remind of Masses, and the import notifies nobody — its intentions have their "status" at once and do not wait in “Entries to accept”.

prompt.task: Copy the Mass intentions from the attached photos of the book of intentions into JSON in the "recreatio/masses" format (description below).
prompt.export: Below is also the export of the parish calendar for this period: all Masses with "date", "time" and "mass" — with the intentions they already have, or with "free": true.
prompt.answer: Return ONE JSON object (without comments): this export with the intentions from the book written into the right items. Do not add or remove items; describe a Mass from the book that is not in the export separately, outside the JSON.
prompt.exact: Copy the text exactly; an illegible word — the best reading and “[?]” at the end of the text. Write the donor and the offering only when they are in the book.
